explain.say: Imagine a player who just waits next to the other team's goal all game, ready to tap in easy goals. Not fair, right? The offside rule stops that. Look at the checklist: when every box is ticked, it is offside.

faq.q: Can you be offside in your own half?
faq.a: No. You can only be in an offside position in the other team's half of the pitch.
asks: Is there offside in your own half?

faq.a: Usually the goalkeeper is the last defender, so the rule needs one more opponent between you and the goal line, or level with you, to keep you onside.
asks: What is the second last opponent?

faq.a: You are offside if, when a teammate passes, you are in the other half, ahead of the ball and past the second-last defender, and then you join the play.
asks: How does the offside rule work?

faq.q: Can you be offside from a throw-in?
faq.a: No. There is no offside from a throw-in, a goal kick or a corner kick.
asks: Is there offside from a corner?

faq.q: What happens when a player is offside?
faq.a: The referee stops play and gives the other team an indirect free kick from where the offside player was.
asks: What is the punishment for offside?

facts: Under Law 11, a player level with the second-last opponent is not in an offside position.
A player cannot be offside directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.
